newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Syria urges U.S. to pressure Israel for talks.
newsitem.headline: Syria urges U.S. to pressure Israel for talks.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on Monday called on the United States to put pressure on its close ally Israel to resume soon talks with Damascus.

"Syria is ready for the talks with Israel on the condition that the negotiations begin from the point where they broke (last year)," Khaddam told reporters shortly after his arrival at Morocco's Rabat airport.
He was met by Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and other government officials.

Khaddam, on a tour of North African countries accompanied by Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, is expected to meet King Hassan on Monday evening at the royal palace in Rabat, a Moroccan official said.
"Syria expects his majesty King Hassan's support for Syria's stand in the Middle East peace process," al-Shara said.
Khaddam reiterated that Damascus would resume negotiations with the Jewish state only after Israel agreed to return the Golan Heights, which it captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Asked about a United States' role in possible Israeli-Syrian negotiations, Khaddam said: "We are ready for the negotiations but it is up to the United States to convince Israel to respect its previous commitments."
Israel broke off talks after a wave of Islamist bombings in Israel last February and March.
A resumption of talks is stymied by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to negotiate the return of land.
Khaddam excluded the possibility of an Arab summit being held in the coming months "because no new elements in the Middle East peace process have emerged which necessitate a summit."
The next Arab summit is scheduled to be held in Damascus in support of Syria's stand, a Moroccan official said.
The Syrian delegation earlier visited Algeria and Mauritania and on Tuesday will visit Libya and then Tunisia, a Syrian diplomat said.
